source.license_note: Real upstream goccy/go-json optimization PR #345; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up JSON string decoding so unescaping a string with many escape sequences stops repeatedly re-allocating and shifting the underlying buffer, without changing decoded output.
task.instructions: Optimize the internal/decoder string-unescaping path for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark Benchmark306 measures decoding a string with many escapes; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: unescapeString rewrites the buffer with repeated append/copy and bytes.IndexByte scans per escape, re-shifting the tail on every escape so decoding a string with many escapes is quadratic.

ops_fault.description: Decoding JSON strings that contain many escape sequences is slow because unescapeString in internal/decoder/string.go repeatedly appends and copies the buffer tail for each escape instead of unescaping in place.
repair_keywords: unescape in place with src/dst pointers

visible_context.issue_text: Decoding a JSON string that contains a large number of escape sequences is unexpectedly slow because the unescape step re-shifts the remaining buffer for each escape it processes.
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization PR #345; the slow path is the per-escape append/copy in unescapeString.
